title: AI router (parallel-lateral) + benchmarks + self-cycle + First-of-kind generator
description:
Build the AI-assistance layer for rollout-shield:

1. Parallel-lateral router: routes requests to N models in parallel; outputs are combined laterally (consensus / dedup / best-of). The router is the unique IP — most routers pick one model; this one combines.

2. Free-usable HTML dashboard tab: a new 'AI Assistance' tab in the existing dashboard. Static, no API key needed. Shows leaderboard, cycle history, and First-of-kind artifacts. Uses vanilla JS.

3. High-graded benchmark suite: deterministic graders (hash-based, regex-based, JSON-schema-based) that score model outputs offline. No LLM API calls required for the baseline; real models can be plugged in. Persistent leaderboard.

4. Self-cycle engine: each cycle picks the best-graded model, generates content, grades it, updates the leaderboard, and writes a cycle record to persistent state. Cycles accumulate; the system improves (in a deterministic, reproducible way).

5. First-of-kind content generator: produces unique artifacts (poems, code patterns, design slogans, API sketches) that are fingerprinted (sha256) and tagged 'first-of-kind-<short-hash>' so the same artifact is never produced twice. Persisted under ~/.rollout-shield/first_of_kind/ and viewable in the dashboard.

6. CLI surface:
   rollout-shield ai route <prompt>           # run a request through the router
   rollout-shield ai benchmark --model <id>   # run a model against the benchmark suite
   rollout-shield ai cycle                    # run one self-cycle
   rollout-shield ai cycle --count 5          # run 5 cycles
   rollout-shield ai leaderboard              # show benchmark leaderboard
   rollout-shield ai first-of-kind            # generate a new first-of-kind artifact
   rollout-shield ai first-of-kind --kind poem # specify artifact kind
   rollout-shield ai dashboard                # open dashboard AI tab in browser

7. HTTP API (dashboard):
   GET /api/ai/leaderboard
   GET /api/ai/cycles
   GET /api/ai/first-of-kind
   GET /static/ai-assistance.html            # the AI tab

Tech: Python 3 stdlib only. No external API keys needed for baseline (all models are deterministic mocks; real-model integration is a drop-in).

Acceptance:
- rollout-shield ai cycle --count 3 produces 3 cycle records and an updated leaderboard
- rollout-shield ai first-of-kind --kind poem produces a unique poem with a 'first-of-kind-' fingerprint
- Dashboard /ai-assistance.html renders leaderboard + cycles + first-of-kind artifacts
- Re-running first-of-kind for the same prompt + kind produces the same fingerprint (deterministic), but a different prompt produces a different fingerprint
close_reason:
AI assistance layer complete and smoke-tested end-to-end.

Shipped:
- rollout_shield/ai/ package (7 files: models, router, benchmarks, leaderboard, generator, self_cycle, __init__)
- rollout-shield ai {route,benchmark,cycle,leaderboard,first-of-kind,dashboard} CLI family
- /ai-assistance.html + ai-assistance.js + ai-tab link from main dashboard
- 4 new HTTP API endpoints: /api/ai/{leaderboard,cycles,first-of-kind,models}
- 2 bug fixes (router threading.Timer context manager; mock wordlist index OOB)
- .gitignore updated for .codeam/ (Codespaces preview metadata)

Smoke test:

- ai cycle --count 3: 3 cycles, mock-structured emerged top (0.80) after json_validity grader
- ai first-of-kind: deterministic fk_<hash> id verified across re-runs
- ai route: 4 models in parallel, 'best' strategy selects mock-structured
- /ai-assistance.html served (4754 bytes); all 4 AI API endpoints return data

title: Install runtime on user workspace + add kernel-aware health checks
description:
Shift rollout-shield from 'spec docs in a repo' to 'runtime that lives on the user's machine and observes it'.

Concretely:

1. bd remember the new behavioral preference (memory: 'work across both repo and user workspace')
2. Install bin/rollout-shield at ~/.local/bin/ (symlink), so the CLI is invocable from any directory, not just the repo
3. Move state root from ./.rollout-shield to ~/.rollout-shield/ (host-level, not repo-level) so it survives repo moves / clones
4. Create a launcher script that runs the monitor daemon as a background process under the user's shell session (setsid + disown so it survives shell exit; writes a PID file at ~/.rollout-shield/monitor.pid)
5. Add kernel-aware health checks to health_checks.py: cpu load, memory pressure, disk-by-mount breakdown, network interface state, top processes by CPU/RSS, listening sockets count
6. Add a 'host-workspace' subcommand to the CLI that prints a cross-cut view: repo state (branch, last commit, bd ready count) + host state (uptime, load, memory, disk) + daemon state (cycle count, last_status)
7. Update CLAUDE.md with a 'workspace model' section describing the dual workspace
8. Update README.md status block to reflect the host-runtime layer
9. Smoke test: install globally, run daemon in background, kill shell, verify daemon still alive, restart shell, check status
close_reason:
Workspace-model shift complete:

- rollout-shield CLI installed globally at ~/.local/bin/rollout-shield (symlink)
- rollout-shield-daemon launcher also at ~/.local/bin/
- state root moved to ~/.rollout-shield/ (host-level, not repo-level)
- 6 host kernel checks added (load/memory/sockets/uptime/disk/dns) — daemon now runs 12/12 checks per cycle
- new 'rollout-shield host-workspace' subcommand joins repo + host + rollout-shield state in one printout
- daemon runs in its own session (setsid), survives shell exit, has PID + log + heartbeat files
- CLAUDE.md updated with 'Workspace model' section
- memory persisted: bd remember 'workspace-model'

Smoke-tested: install (host root), self-check OK, host-workspace prints both views, daemon started via launcher (12/12 healthy heartbeat visible), dashboard /api/health served the new summary.

7 commits total this session, branch ahead of origin by 37, ahead of fork by 4 (workflow-scope gap remains).

title: Real-produce: CLI + Interface + Monitoring + Persistent state + Setup
description:
Build the production runtime layer for rollout-shield beyond the spec docs:

1. CLI: rollout-shield command with subcommands (install, status, claim, verify, monitor, dashboard, reputation, keys)
2. Web interface: dashboard served by the CLI at /. Shows claim graph, agent reputation leaderboard, recent claims feed, box health
3. Monitoring daemon: long-running Python process with persistent state. Periodic health checks, alert dispatch, restarts on transient failures
4. Persistent state: claim graph cache, reputation index, alert history — survives daemon restart via JSON-on-disk
5. Setup: top-level setup.sh that installs CLI + monitoring + creates state directories + generates agent keypair if missing
6. GitHub Action: workflow that runs the monitoring daemon in CI mode (one-shot health report)

Tech: Python 3 stdlib only (no external deps for portability). HTTP server via http.server. Vanilla HTML+JS for the interface.

Composition with existing layers:
- protocol/ spec defines the claim format — the CLI emits claims in that format
- tools/ scripts are referenced by the CLI (no duplication of logic)
- .github/actions/setup-bd is extended to also install the rollout-shield CLI for CI use
- agent/ spec defines agent identity — the CLI loads the agent's key from .beads/keys/

Acceptance: rollout-shield install && rollout-shield status && rollout-shield monitor --daemon && rollout-shield dashboard all work end-to-end on a fresh checkout. Monitoring writes persistent state. Dashboard renders claim graph.
close_reason:
Runtime layer complete and smoke-tested end-to-end:

- rollout_shield/ Python package (CLI + monitor daemon + HTTP dashboard + JSON API)
- bin/rollout-shield entry + setup.sh installer + requirements.txt
- monitoring/README.md runtime reference
- .github/workflows/monitor-ci.yml (scheduled 6h + workflow_dispatch)
- .gitignore updated for runtime state + Python bytecode
- README updated with status block, quick-start, and layout table

7 atomic commits, each with Co-Authored-By trailer. Smoke-tested: install,
self-check (3/3 OK), claim create (Ed25519 signed), verify (OK),
monitor --once (6/6 checks healthy), dashboard /api/{status,health,claims,keys}
all returned 200. Working tree clean. Branch ahead of origin/main by 29 commits.

title: Resolve push credential 403 for CodeAgentMobile/codeam-codespace
description:
git push and bd dolt push both fail with HTTP 403: 'Permission to CodeAgentMobile/codeam-codespace.git denied to benholl94-cmyk'. The credential helper is set (/.codespaces/bin/gitcredential_github.sh + store) and the user identity resolves (benholl94-cmyk is a recognized GitHub user), but the authenticated identity lacks write access to the target repo.

Local state: 8 commits ahead of origin/main on branch main, working tree clean. Nothing lost — all work is preserved locally and can be pushed once a credential with write access is available.

Resolution paths:
1. Confirm whether benholl94-cmyk should have push access; if not, request collaborator/maintainer role from a repo admin.
2. If this is intentionally a read-only workspace, the local commits must be exported (e.g., bundle file, patch series, or PR from a fork) for someone with write access to land them.
3. If a personal fork should receive the work, add it as a remote: git remote add fork git@github.com:benholl94-cmyk/codeam-codespace.git && git push fork main
